title: Root systems on a deep bed at 43,200 frames — blob, or not
question: Do these read as eight different root systems, or as eight of the same thing? And is either one the 'big blob that fills in all space' you flagged?
context_md:
Your direction was: *"There should be a disadvantage for growing a big blob of roots that fully fills in all space. If the root cell isn't touching soil it cannot benefit the plant and has a cost... we don't want to force the roots to grow a certain way but set up a system that leads to interesting and heterogenous results."*

One of these is the current build. In the other, a root cell that shares no face with soil earns the plant nothing — it buys no water storage — and still costs food to keep. **Nothing anywhere says what shape a root should be.**

Worth knowing before you judge: the measurement said this would be a **flat tax on root mass, not a brake on it**, and that is what happened — the root system is 73% smaller and the fraction of it touching soil barely moved (64.6% to 65.6%). So the question is really about *shape and variety*, not about efficiency.

100-row soil bed, same eight founders, same frame.
